title: Kernel shim for amortized cast elimination during streaming attention
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Implement a small kernel shim + scheduler heuristic that eliminates redundant tensor casts (int8<->fp16/fp8) across streaming attention prefill and decode phases by tracking per-KV-lane precision state and performing opportunistic zero-cost reuse. Goal is to reduce dequant/requant overhead without compromising correctness or introducing tail latency regressions.
acceptance_criteria: No correctness regressions on unit and integration tests for gpt-neox-20b and multilingual-7b baseline suites
End-to-end 95th-percentile latency improvement >= 8% on short decode (<=64 tokens) workloads compared to baseline with naive casts
Memory overhead < 3% for KV metadata bookkeeping
Can be toggled per-model via config and has telemetry hooks for cast-skips and fallbacks
design_notes: Shim sits between kernel selector and runtime dispatcher; maintains a compact per-head-per-layer precision tag for KV entries
On prefill we prefer path binding: if initial layer compute uses INT8->FP16 fusion kernel, mark the KV lane as INT8-compatible; on decode, skip cast if kernel chosen supports streaming INT8 acc
Fallback policy: if a downstream kernel needs higher precision (FP8/FP16) we emit a single batched dequant for affected lanes and mark a local cooldown to avoid oscillation
Tradeoffs considered: additional metadata adds bookeeping cost and complexity in scheduler; chosen compact 8-bit tag scheme minimizes memory while allowing TTL semantics
We decided against global conservative probing because it increased read amplification and regressed throughput for large-batch workloads
implementation_plan: Phase 1: Minimal shim + unit tests for precision tag lifecycle (2 spikes, unit tests) — complete
Phase 2: Integrate shim with kernel selector and add policy flags; end-to-end perf harness runs (in progress)
Phase 3: Canary rollout on dedicated infra with telemetry gating and automated rollback rule; collect real traffic metrics
Phase 4: Iterate heuristics based on telemetry and extend to multi-precision (INT8/FP8/FP16) paths
benchmarks: Local microbench: 11% median decode latency win, 9% 95p win for 32-token streams on a-prod-gpu-rt with gpt-neox-20b quantized path
End-to-end scenario (chatbot-sim): 7.2% cost-per-token reduction measured on sustained 200RPS workload with KV reuse
Edge case: when models frequently switch precision per-layer, observed a 1.9% increase in tail latency before adding cooldown — fixed by cooldown window
qa_and_tests: Unit tests for tag encode/decode across endianness and alignment
Integration tests including simulated model rollovers that change precision mid-sequence
Fuzz harness for scheduler to verify no path introduces double-free or stale-kv reads
Stability run: 48h soak with canary traffic that asserts no more than 0.1% error-rate increase
comments: 2026-02-11 Aisha Patel: Spike complete — prototype shim successfully avoids cast in single-layer streaming decode. Added unit tests for tag rollover.
2026-02-18 Marco Li: Integrated shim with kernel selector. Observed regressions on large-batch (>512 tokens) prefill due to extra conditional checks — optimized branchless tag lookup to mitigate.
2026-02-26 QA: Found a race when two concurrent requests try to mark same KV lane precision; added per-lane lightweight lock (compare-exchange) and regression tests.

2026-03-03 Perf: Canary run shows stable 95p improvement for chat workloads; however, an internal A/B test uncovered a ~2% throughput regression for batched embedding endpoints — scoped and disabled shim for non-attention routes.
2026-03-09 Review (SRE): Asked for stronger telemetry on fallback events and an automated alert when fallback rate > 0.5% — added counters and alert rule in grafana/principals.
